question.prompt: For each real number \(a\) with \(0 \le a \le 1,\) let numbers \(x\) and \(y\) be chosen independently at random from the intervals \([0, a]\) and \([0, 1],\) respectively, and let \(P(a)\) be the probability that \[\sin^2(\pi x) + \sin^2(\pi y) \gt 1.\] What is the maximum value of \(P(a)?\)

solutions.title: Find the favorable region
solutions.explanation:
Although the condition involves sine, its boundary in the unit square consists of straight lines. This lets us calculate the probability using triangle areas.

Use the usual continuous uniform interpretation of choosing from each interval. When \(a>0\), independence makes \((x,y)\) uniform in the rectangle \([0,a]\times[0,1]\), whose area is \(a\). At \(a=0\), interpret the degenerate interval as \(x=0\) with certainty. Then the strict inequality is impossible, so \(P(0)=0\).

The identity \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) turns the desired condition into
\[
\sin^2(\pi x)>\cos^2(\pi y).
\]
Set \(t=\min(x,1-x)\), so \(0\le t\le\frac12\). The trigonometric reduction formulas give
\[
\sin(\pi x)=\sin(\pi t),\qquad
|\cos(\pi y)|=\sin\!\left(\pi\left|y-\frac12\right|\right).
\]
Both sine values are nonnegative, and sine is strictly increasing on \([0,\pi/2]\). Therefore the condition is exactly
\[
\left|y-\frac12\right|<\min(x,1-x).
\]
This describes the interior of the diamond with vertices \((0,\frac12),(\frac12,0),(1,\frac12),(\frac12,1)\). Its boundary has area zero, so excluding the boundary does not affect the probability.

If \(0<a\le\frac12\), the favorable region is a triangle with vertical base \(2a\) at \(x=a\) and horizontal height \(a\). Hence
\[
P(a)=\frac{\frac12(2a)a}{a}=a\le\frac12.
\]

Now suppose \(\frac12\le a\le1\). It is easier to subtract the unfavorable area. To the left of \(x=\frac12\), the unfavorable parts are two right triangles, each with legs \(\frac12\), giving total area \(\frac14\). Between \(x=\frac12\) and \(x=a\), there are two more right triangles, each with legs \(a-\frac12\), giving total area \((a-\frac12)^2\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(a)
&=1-\frac{\frac14+(a-\frac12)^2}{a}\\
&=2-a-\frac{1}{2a}.
\end{aligned}
\]
By AM-GM, the sum of two positive numbers is at least twice the square root of their product, so
\[
a+\frac{1}{2a}\ge2\sqrt{a\cdot\frac{1}{2a}}=\sqrt2.
\]
Equality holds when \(a=\frac{1}{2a}\), namely \(a=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\), which lies in \([\frac12,1]\). Therefore this range has maximum \(2-\sqrt2\). Since \(2-\sqrt2>\frac12\), it also exceeds every value from the earlier range.

The overall maximum is \(\boxed{2-\sqrt2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Optimize the second probability piece by AM-GM
